title: The 7-Day Prevention Reset
subtitle: A Gentle One-Week Plan for Building Healthier Everyday Habits

pages.title: A reset is not a cleanse
pages.body: This reset means pausing, observing, and creating a few useful routines. It is not a detox, crash diet, or promise.
bullets: Do not change medicines or insulin based on this guide.
Choose movement that is safe for your body.

pages.title: How habits work
pages.body: Habits often need a cue, a routine, and a reward. The smaller the routine, the easier it is to repeat when life gets busy.
bullets: Tie a new habit to something you already do.
Make backup plans part of the habit.

pages.title: Seven-day overview
pages.body: Each day asks for one main action. You can repeat a day, skip a day, or adapt the plan. The point is learning, not proving anything.
bullets: Day 1 notice.
Day 2 build one balanced meal.
Day 3 add fiber.
Day 4 break up sitting.
Day 5 improve one drink.
Day 6 protect sleep.
Day 7 plan next week.

pages.title: Notice your starting point
pages.body: Record a normal day without judgment. Notice drinks, meals, movement, sleep, energy, mood, and one thing that felt hard.
bullets: Choose one realistic goal.
Keep private health notes secure.

pages.title: Build one balanced meal
pages.body: Use the Mindful Plate method for one meal only. Add vegetables, protein, carbohydrate, and a lower-sugar drink if possible.
bullets: One meal is enough.
Mixed dishes can still count.

pages.title: Add a source of fiber
pages.body: Add one fiber source such as beans, lentils, oats, berries, vegetables, whole grains, nuts, or seeds. Increase gradually and drink fluids.
bullets: Stop and ask for advice if fiber worsens symptoms.
People with some medical diets need individual guidance.

pages.title: Break up sitting time
pages.body: Short activity breaks can help many people. Options include walking, standing, chair movement, stretching, or gentle household tasks.
bullets: The CDC describes 150 minutes per week as a common adult activity goal, but starting slowly is okay. [9]
Ask which activities are safest for you.

pages.title: Improve one drink
pages.body: Choose one drink you have often and adjust it. Try less sugar, a smaller size, unsweet tea, water, sparkling water, or a gradual step-down.
bullets: You do not need to love plain water overnight.
Alcohol and diabetes medicine require safety awareness.

pages.title: Protect sleep
pages.body: A realistic sleep routine may include a consistent wake time, dimmer light, less late caffeine, a wind-down cue, and a plan for pain, caregiving, or work shifts.
bullets: Sleep problems deserve care, not blame.
Ask about snoring, breathing pauses, insomnia, or restless legs.

pages.title: Prepare the next week
pages.body: Look back at what helped, what felt irritating, and what was too much. Pick one habit to repeat for another week.
bullets: Keep the habit small.
Write down one question for a clinician if needed.

pages.title: Hydration tracker
pages.body: Track drinks for awareness, not judgment. A beverage inventory can reveal one easy place to reduce added sugar.
callout: Store completed health notes securely if they include personal information.

pages.title: Movement tracker
pages.body: Record movement that is safe for your body. Chair movement, stretching, physical therapy exercises, and short walks all count as information.

pages.title: Meal and fiber tracker
pages.body: Use this page to notice meals that kept you satisfied. Write the vegetable, protein, carbohydrate, and fiber source when you can.

pages.title: Sleep check-in
pages.body: Sleep is affected by stress, shift work, caregiving, pain, medications, breathing problems, and mental health. This page helps you notice what is changeable.

pages.title: Mood and energy
pages.body: Energy can change with meals, sleep, movement, stress, and blood glucose. A simple mood and energy note can help you see patterns.

pages.title: Optional glucose notes
pages.body: If you monitor glucose, use this page only in the way your care team recommends. Do not chase perfect numbers.
callout: Record action taken according to your care plan. Do not change medicine based on this worksheet alone.

pages.title: Obstacles and backup plans
pages.body: Plan for busy days before they arrive. A backup meal, safe movement option, and lower-sugar drink can protect momentum.

fields: What I can let be imperfect

pages.title: 30-day continuation plan
pages.body: After seven days, continue one or two habits. A prevention plan should fit real life well enough to survive an ordinary month.

pages.title: Repeat what worked
pages.body: Keep one or two helpful routines. Drop what was unrealistic. Add one next step only when the current habit feels repeatable.
bullets: Explore other Mindful Diabetes guides.
Visit Health Tools.
Ask your care team about patterns you noticed.
